modes.name: Explore
modes.summary: Pick a place, press Play: hear how its ozone, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides or rain changes over time.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Pick a dataset with the Data menu (ozone, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides from NASA's GEOS-CF model, or IMERG rain): the map shows it and you hear only it, on its own recorded instrument and pitch range (carbon monoxide cello low, ozone flute in the middle, nitrogen oxides koto higher, rain marimba). Higher values play higher notes. Click, tap or use the arrow keys to pick a place (hovering only announces), then press Play: the map animates and the place's value plays as a melody, one note per hour. With no place picked, Play uses New Delhi.

modes.name: Flow tracers
modes.summary: NASA IMERG rain with particles following its motion. Press Play: tracers over rain sing, heavier rain higher and louder.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: NASA's real-time precipitation (IMERG) over the continents, with streams of particles following the rain's motion. Yellow tracers over rain sing: heavier rain plays higher and louder, west to east pans left to right.

modes.name: Precipitation ball
modes.summary: A ball rolls over a terrain raised by NASA IMERG rain, and its motion makes the sound.
modes.author: itay
modes.description: Place a ball on the moving IMERG precipitation video; rain raises a terrain whose slope rolls the ball around, with Web Audio sound following its motion. Keyboard: focus the map, Enter places the ball, arrows move it. From itay's clustering branch.

modes.name: Scanning line
modes.summary: A line sweeps one NASA IMERG rain map west to east and plays it: low notes at the bottom, high at the top, louder where it rains harder.
modes.author: itay
modes.description: A line sweeps across one global IMERG precipitation frame from west to east and plays it as notes on a C major scale, low (C2) at the bottom of the map and high (C5) at the top; the heaviest rain in each band sets that note's volume. From itay's scanning-line-demo branch.

modes.name: Storm watch
modes.summary: Storms in NASA IMERG rain data, tracked over 24 hours. Click a storm or press N to hear it: north sounds higher, bigger storms louder.
modes.author: itay
modes.description: Follow individual storms through 48 half-hourly IMERG frames, tracked offline with computer vision (OpenCV optical flow and watershed). Click a storm, or press N and P on the map, to hear it (hovering only names it): north sounds higher, bigger storms louder. Enter follows a storm, and when storms merge and split the whole family stays marked; Page Up and Page Down step through time. The full tracking studio with tuning sliders is linked from the panel. From itay's clustering branch.

modes.name: Tone lab
modes.summary: A world map of instruments: click a region to hear its note, scale, chord or phrase, once or on a loop.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Every region of the world has its own instrument. Click or tap a region, or use the arrow keys and Enter, to hear a note, a scale, a chord or its typical phrase, once or on a loop. Recorded and analysed instruments are in the Instrument list.

modes.name: Vortex melodies
modes.summary: Swirling storms in NASA IMERG rain: press Play and every swirl loops its own tune, faster spin plays faster and the dot circles once per tune. Click or press Enter on a swirl to hear it alone; Escape brings back all.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Swirling storms in NASA real-time precipitation (IMERG), found by optical flow and tracked over the day. Each swirl loops a short tune: faster spin plays faster, bigger swirls louder; a low hum swells where rain converges.

modes.name: World orchestra
modes.summary: The world's musical regions on one map, each with its own recorded instrument. Click or use the arrow keys to hear a region; turn Instruments off and press Play to hear cities play the data.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: The world's musical regions on one map. Instruments (on at first): click, tap, or use the arrow keys, and each region plays a short phrase on a recorded instrument (djembe, kora, oud, balalaika, khomus, morin khuur, sitar, koto, pan flute...); moving the mouse into a region plays it too. Turn it off and about 280 cities play the data you pick in the Data menu (ozone, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides or rain): a city whose value rises past a threshold plays one note in its region's voice.
